prose.headline: Comstock: buy $14.24 on its 50-day hold, eyeing the $15.22 weekly high by Oct 27, cut under $13.91.
story: Comstock Resources is basing after a long fall. It trades at 51% of its 52-week high of $28.10 from Dec 5, 2025 and has won back only 13% of the drop, but the low end has firmed: the Oct 1 spring under the 40-day low reversed, the 20-day retest held on Oct 16, and the latest session held the 50-day at $13.91 with a three outside up candle pattern. Price at $14.24 is above the 10-day at $13.81, the 20-day at $13.40 and the 20-day VWAP at $13.44. The falling 200-day at $16.52 is the bigger ceiling, with the weekly swing high at $15.22 first.

Momentum is building from a low base: RSI rose to 57 from 55, MACD is above zero and over its signal line with the gap widening, and a hidden bullish divergence on MACD sits under the turn. Volume ran near normal at 0.95× on the day, and the accumulation/distribution line shows a regular bullish divergence, so the base is being bought rather than chased. The business is the drag, with revenue down 24.9% and profit down to $8.8M from $124.8M, and the weekly trend still slopes down, which keeps the target close at the weekly swing high. The daily and hourly trends point up and QQQ gained 1.21% last session, enough of a tailwind for a run to that level.
prose.play: Buy $14.10 to $14.24 now, on the 50-day hold; the target is $15.22, the weekly swing high, by Oct 27, and a daily close under $13.91, the 50-day itself, voids the call.

prose.headline: National Presto: buy $150.41 on the averages, back toward the $158.17 high by Oct 27, wrong under $147.43.
story: National Presto is sitting on a shelf of averages just below its highs. The 10-day at $148.73, the 20-day at $148.40 and the 50-day at $148.30 have converged under price, and both the 20-day and 50-day retests held in the latest session, which closed at $150.41 with a narrow-range candle near the high. The 50-day has risen from $139.44 in a month, the 200-day at $135.20 trails below, and the last swing low at $142.60 is the deeper floor. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $154.50 comes first, then the 52-week high of $158.17 from Aug 25, where the Aug 26 upthrust failed.

Every timeframe points up, weekly, daily and hourly, and the stock leads the S&P 500 by 20.7 points and its sector by 29.8 points over three months. RSI ticked up to 54 from 52 with a hidden bullish divergence on MACD, and although MACD sits under its signal line, it is above zero and the gap is narrowing, a pause rather than a turn. Volume was a touch under normal at 0.85×, the 20-day VWAP at $148.19 sits right under price, and the busiest price at $151.87 is just overhead. Revenue grew 21.7% and profit tripled to $15.9M from $5.2M. That is a leader resting on its averages with the high in sight.

story: Amazon reclaimed the 20-day at $253.40 and the 50-day at $256.80 in one 5.0% session, closing at $262.45 near the high of the day. That move came off a cluster of four levels between $254.20 and $259.10, and three of the last four swings have been higher, with the last swing low at $244.30. The 200-day at $242.90 is rising underneath, and the Fibonacci 38.2% level of the swing from $287.20 sits at $252.40, well below. The 52-week high of $287.20 from Aug 3 is the bigger ceiling, with the resistance zone starting at $273.80 first.

The volume was real at 1.62× normal, the candle was a bullish belt hold with a kicker right at the busiest price of $261.14, and on-balance volume is rising with price. RSI jumped to 57 from 45 and MACD is above zero and over its signal line with the gap widening, so momentum has turned up hard. Buyers anchored to the Jul 30 earnings sit right at break-even near $259.12, which makes a close under that VWAP the end of the trade. Revenue grew 19.6% and profit reached $62,647.0M from $18,164.0M. Daily and hourly trends point up, QQQ added 1.21% in the last session and the VIX is calm at 18, so the backdrop supports a run toward the resistance zone.

prose.headline: Newell Brands: buy the Fibonacci midpoint near $5.11 by Oct 26, target $5.62 by Nov 4, void below $4.86.
story: Newell Brands rallied from $3.07 to a 52-week high of $7.13 on Jul 31 and has spent the autumn handing back part of it. The swing structure still steps up, with higher highs and higher lows and the Oct 1 spring under the 40-day low marking the last shakeout. Price closed at $5.54, just under the 20-day at $5.55 and the 50-day at $5.80. It is still sitting right on the rising support line near $5.50 and well above the 200-day at $4.78. The Fibonacci halfway point of the run sits at $5.10, and the support zone from $4.86 to $4.96 lies below it.

The selling is thin: volume ran just 0.55× normal on the day and 0.64× over ten sessions, even as the last candle printed a bearish marubozu at the bottom of the high-volume range. RSI has eased to 47 from 51, but it carries a hidden bullish divergence, the accumulation line shows the same, and MACD is below zero yet back above its signal line. Profit more than doubled to $106.0M from $46.0M on revenue up 3.0%, and the last earnings drew a strong reaction. Holders since the Jul 31 report are 6.5% under their average, so the high-volume range overhead is where the first sellers wait, which is why the objective is its bottom edge.

prose.headline: Wix.com: sell into $79.29 under the Fibonacci ceiling by Oct 23, $70.08 targeted by Nov 2, wrong above $82.48.
story: Wix.com is still badly damaged on the bigger chart: it trades at 52% of its 52-week high of $148.33 from Oct 31, 2025 and has won back only 34% of the drop to $40.16. The recent swings turned the wrong way, a lower high and then a lower low at $67.50, and the Sep 2 upthrust over the 40-day high failed. Price lost the 50-day at $77.43 on Oct 16 and closed at $76.98, while the falling 200-day at $71.32 and the 20-day at $74.59 sit just below. Overhead, the Fibonacci 38.2% level at $81.48 caps the rebound, with the weekly swing high at $80.95 right under it.

The bounce off the 20-day has little behind it: volume was 0.85× normal on the day and only 0.74× over ten sessions, and stochastic is curling over at 66. RSI at 52 and a MACD barely above zero describe a stock drifting, not trending, with daily trend strength weak. Its October record is weak, and the last decisive move was the breakaway gap down in May that has since filled. A pin-bar rejection at the busiest price and recent insider buying explain the bounce, and the short waits for it to run into the weekly swing high and stall. Wix.com is held long by the desk's strategy, so this card takes the other side.

prose.headline: ArcBest: short the retest of $131.95 by Oct 23, objective $124.06 by Oct 30, out on a close over $135.41.
story: ArcBest has lost its footing. It closed at $128.18, under the last swing low, under the 50-day exponential average at $133.37, and below the 20-day at $129.40. The 50-day at $133.80 is sliding from $141.61 a month ago, and on the weekly chart price sits under both the 10-week and the 30-week. From the 52-week high of $176.69 on Jun 12 it now trades at 73% of that peak, with the Fibonacci 38.2% level at $131.90 and the busiest price at $135.41 forming the ceiling right overhead.

Momentum is soft and getting softer: RSI slipped to 44 from 47, the last session closed near its low at the bottom of the high-volume range, and the stock trails the S&P 500 by 22.8 points over three months. Holders since the Jul 29 earnings are 5.8% under their $136.12 average and trapped after a weak reaction, and the company swung to a $13.8M loss from a $25.8M profit even with revenue up 15.9%. Volume on the down day was only 0.52× normal, so the drift lower has not flushed anyone yet. MACD has curled above its signal line and the Sep 28 spring held, which sets up the bounce into $131.95 that gets sold. the desk's strategy is long and has the stock queued, the other side of this card.
prose.play: If the bounce stalls between $131.95 and $134.12 by Oct 23, short it; the objective is $124.06, the 20-session low, by Oct 30, and a daily close over $135.41 at the busiest price voids it.

prose.headline: Celsius: long a dip to $29.11 by Oct 23, aiming $31.10 by Oct 30, cancelled by a close under $28.43.
story: Celsius is trying to turn a long slide into a base. It trades far below its 52-week high of $66.00 and has won back only 14% of the drop from $66.74, but three of the last four swings were higher and the last swing low at $26.43 held this month. The latest session was a bullish engulfing outside bar that closed near its high and reclaimed the 50-day at $29.31, with the 20-day at $27.97 now underneath. Overhead, the falling 200-day at $35.53 and the weekly swing high at $30.27 cap the bigger picture, and the weekly trend still points down.

Momentum has flipped up: RSI jumped to 58 from 50, and MACD, while still below zero, has crossed back above its signal line, with a hidden bullish divergence on MACD behind it. The day's volume was close to normal at 1.06× after ten slow sessions at 0.66×, and on-balance volume is rising with price. A cluster of four levels sits between $28.06 and $28.80, a heavy-volume shelf with the 20-day inside it, and buyers anchored to the Aug 6 earnings are 3.6% in profit. Revenue grew 10.6% even as profit fell to $55.3M from $99.9M. The hourly trend points up while the weekly still slopes down, which keeps the objective close, at the top of the high-volume range.

prose.headline: Campbell's: the pop toward $19.82 is for selling until Oct 23, with $18.74 next by Oct 30; void over $20.38.
story: Campbell's has been sliding for a year and now sits just above its 52-week low of $18.60. From the Nov 21, 2025 high of $32.04 it has won back only 6% of the drop, and holders anchored to that high are down 17% at an average of $23.21. A rising wedge that formed after May 21 broke to the downside, and price now sits under the 50-day exponential average at $20.70, the 20-day at $19.55, the falling 50-day at $21.32 and the falling 200-day at $22.72. The 50-day has rolled from $22.43 in a month, and both the weekly and daily trends point down.

Momentum is rolling over again: RSI dropped to 42 from 47, and the accumulation/distribution line carries a bearish divergence, so the distribution is real. Ten-session volume has run 1.36× normal on the way down, and the stock trails its sector by 17.1 points over three months after a weak earnings reaction and a 4.4% drop in revenue. The Oct 8 spring under the 40-day low and a MACD back above its signal line explain the small bounces, and stochastic is high at 89, which leaves little fuel for another one. Selling a failed pop into the 2-session high is the trade, with the earnings VWAP as the line. the desk's strategy is long and has Campbell's queued, the other side of this card.

story: Donnelley Financial just confirmed a double bottom. The breakout over the $51.31 neckline came last week, and the retest in the latest session held, with price closing at $52.24. That completes an 80% recovery of the slide from $56.26 to $36.11, and the measured move of the pattern points right back to the 52-week high of $56.26 from Jan 16. Every average sits under price and in order, the 10-day first, then the 20-day at $49.05 and the 50-day at $48.62. The 200-day at $47.07 and the support line near $48.02 hold beneath them.

Every timeframe points up, weekly, daily and hourly, and momentum is accelerating: RSI rose to 64 from 63 and MACD is above zero and over its signal line with the gap widening. The pattern was built on solid ground, with the busiest price at $48.35 and buyers since the Jul 30 earnings in profit above $48.48. The retest came on 0.81× normal volume, which is how a clean breakout pauses. The weak spots are distance and calendar: price is stretched 2.3 daily ranges above the 50-day, the weekly swing high at $53.56 sits just overhead, and the October record is weak, which is why the objective is the recent swing high rather than the measured move.

prose.headline: Frontdoor is a buy at $79.84 into the busiest price, with $85.32 the target by Oct 29; wrong under $78.12.
story: Frontdoor is pressing back into the middle of its range after a clean higher low. The last swing low at $70.25 held, the Sep 24 spring shook out the weak hands, and the reclaim of the 20-day at $76.60 on Oct 15 has held since. Price closed at $79.84, right at the busiest price of $79.81 and a hair under the 50-day at $79.85. The 10-day at $78.53 and a support zone from $77.34 to $78.81 sit directly beneath. The rising support line near $72.76 and the 200-day at $68.27 back the whole structure, and the 52-week high of $93.43 from Aug 7 is the bigger magnet.

The push came on 1.37× normal volume, MACD crossed above zero on Oct 19 and sits over its signal line with the gap widening, and RSI rose to 56 from 53. On-balance volume and the accumulation/distribution line both confirm, the latter with a hidden bullish divergence. Buyers since the Aug 6 earnings are flat at $79.93, so the supply from that crowd is thin, and the stock leads its sector by 9.4 points over three months with revenue up 4.5% and profit at $125.0M from $111.0M. The only shelf in the way is the weekly swing high at $80.73, and above it the top of the high-volume range is open.

prose.headline: Hexcel: buy the support-zone dip to $90.24 by Oct 23, objective $95.22 by Nov 2, void under $87.56.
story: Hexcel has given back more than a third of its run from $60.82 to $111.70 and is now trying to turn back up. The Jul 27 upthrust at the 52-week high of $111.74 marked the top, but the swings since have reset higher, with higher highs and higher lows and the last swing low at $82.69. The 20-day retest held on Oct 14, and the latest session reclaimed the 50-day at $91.15 and closed at $91.61, with the 200-day at $90.53 and the 10-day at $87.05 right below. Overhead sit the Fibonacci 38.2% level at $92.29 and the earnings VWAP at $92.99, which is why the entry is lower, on the support zone.

The reclaim had real volume behind it, 1.53× normal, and the candle closed near its high right at the 50-day. RSI climbed to 62 from 58, and MACD, still below zero, is well above its signal line, so momentum is improving from a low base. On-balance volume is rising with price, and profit jumped to $49.3M from $13.5M on revenue up 8.0%. The weekly chart is the caution: it still carries negative divergences and a distribution phase, and the stock trails the S&P 500 by 18.1 points over three months. A first move to the weekly swing high fits that picture, bought on a dip into the support zone.

prose.headline: monday.com: buy a dip to $90.94 until Oct 23, aiming for $97.30 by Oct 29; finished below $87.67.
story: monday.com is rebuilding after a brutal year, trading at 44% of its 52-week high of $210.49 from Nov 3, 2025 with only 24% of the drop won back. The recent base is doing the work: the Sep 30 spring under the 40-day low reversed, the 20-day retest held on Oct 14, and the latest session held the 50-day at $88.61 and closed at $93.42, up 3.4%. The 10-day at $88.07 and the 200-day at $85.34 sit underneath, and the long support line near $74.57 has three touches. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $95.46 is the first shelf.

The base has momentum and real support: RSI rose to 58 from 55, MACD crossed above zero on Oct 15 and sits well over its signal line, and on-balance volume is rising with price. The last candles, an inside bar and a bullish harami at the support zone, show buyers defending the dip, and three desk strategies fired on the name. The stock leads the S&P 500 by 25.8 points over three months. Two things argue for a lower entry: volume on the up day was light at 0.78× normal, and momentum divergences on MACD and money flow have been flagging the rallies, so the trade is a pullback buy toward the last session's low, not a chase.

prose.headline: Devon Energy is a buy at $50.92 above its high-volume range, with $52.71 targeted by Oct 26; wrong below $50.25.
story: Devon Energy is pressing against its 52-week high of $52.71 from Mar 30, and every timeframe, weekly, daily and hourly, points up. Three of the last four swings were higher, from the last swing low at $45.56, and the retests of the 20-day on Oct 9 and the 50-day on Oct 7 both held. The averages are stacked in order beneath price, the 10-day at $49.31, the 20-day at $48.31, the 50-day at $48.12 and the 200-day at $45.31. The support line near $46.94 has been touched three times, and price closed at $50.92, just over the top of the high-volume range at $50.25.

Momentum is building: RSI rose to 63 from 62, and MACD crossed above zero and its signal line on Oct 8 with the gap widening since. Revenue jumped 73.1% and profit more than doubled to $1,911.0M from $899.0M, and buyers since the Aug 4 earnings are in profit above $47.76. The flags are quiet ones: volume was light at 0.69× normal, the weekly picture shows signs of distribution, and the weekly swing high at $51.41 sits just overhead, so the target stays at the old high rather than beyond it. The last candle was a pin-bar rejection that still closed near the high, which keeps the push intact.

prose.headline: Freshpet: buy $66.12 at the halfway mark of its slide, $69.58 targeted by Oct 26, out under $64.46.
story: Freshpet has won back exactly half of its fall from the 52-week high of $86.00 on Mar 5 to $46.45, and it is sitting right on that Fibonacci 50% level at $66.23. The base underneath has built in steps: the Sep 29 spring under the 40-day low reversed, the last swing low at $56.00 held, and the 20-day retest on Oct 12 held at $62.10. The latest session gapped lower on ordinary volume and slipped just under the 50-day at $66.50, closing at $66.12 on the 10-day at $65.52. The 200-day at $63.71 and a support zone from $62.65 to $64.08 sit beneath.

Momentum is resting rather than breaking: RSI eased to 58 from 60, while MACD is above zero and over its signal line, and three bullish divergences, one of them weekly, sit under the base along with a bullish divergence in money flow. Volume on the down day was light at 0.60× normal, so the gap lower drew no real selling. The stock leads its sector by 13.2 points over three months, revenue grew 15.5%, profit rose to $19.5M from $16.4M, and the last earnings drew a strong reaction. The near overhead is crowded, with the weekly swing high at $66.47 and the earnings VWAP at $67.08, so the target stays at the 20-session high.

prose.headline: Intuit: buy a retreat to $309.71 by Oct 23, with the $336.26 high next by Nov 3; void under $298.83.
story: Intuit is still down at 47% of its 52-week high of $689.17 from Oct 27, 2025, but the daily chart has turned into a base. The Sep 29 spring under the 40-day low reversed fast, MACD crossed back above zero on Oct 16, and the latest session dipped to the 50-day at $321.00 and closed at $325.62 with a wick-rejection candle off it. The 10-day at $309.25 and the 20-day at $294.30 rise beneath, and a support zone runs from $303.50 to $311.00. The falling 200-day at $373.70 is the bigger ceiling, and the 6-month loss of 20% shows how much repair is still ahead.

Momentum supports the base: RSI holds at 61, MACD is over its signal line, and two bullish divergences, one on the weekly chart, sit under the turn. On-balance volume is rising, buyers since the Aug 25 earnings are up 3.4% at an average of $314.76, and three desk strategies fired. Profit grew to $3,064.0M from $2,820.0M on revenue up 10.4%, and the stock leads the S&P 500 by 9.9 points over three months. The latest session's volume was light at 0.71× normal and stochastic is high at 94, so the better entry is a pullback into the support zone, with the 20-session high as the target.

prose.headline: Coty: buy a slip to $2.95 by Oct 26, then a run at $3.28 by Nov 6; ends under $2.86.
story: Coty has pushed through the last swing high at $3.09 and now sits at $3.19. It has won back 52% of its fall from $4.47 to $1.82, and price is just above the Fibonacci halfway mark at $3.15. The averages have turned up in order beneath it, the 10-day at $2.96, the 20-day at $2.81 and the 50-day at $2.77, with the 200-day at $2.52 lower still. The 20-day and 50-day retests both held this month, and the Sep 21 spring under the 40-day low marked the turn. A support zone from $3.04 to $3.11 and the top of the high-volume range at $2.86 frame the pullback.

The trend is strong but extended: RSI is 74, a touch off 75, MACD is above zero and over its signal line, and on-balance volume keeps pointing up. Price is stretched 3.5 daily ranges above the 50-day, further than 92% of its past year, and volume has been light at 0.67× normal on the day and 0.69× over ten sessions, so the next leg needs a reset first. The stock leads its sector by 16.4 points over three months, but the business is not helping, with revenue down 1.3%, a $408.1M loss and a weak earnings reaction. Buying the dip near the 5-session low keeps the risk tight above the high-volume range.

prose.headline: Eli Lilly: buy the close over $1,249.00 by Oct 23, run to $1,292.65 by Oct 28, wrong under $1,239.20.
story: Eli Lilly is pressed right under its breakout level. The swings keep stepping up, higher highs over higher lows from the last swing low at $1,113.00, and the 50-day reclaim and 20-day retest on Oct 14 both held. Price closed at $1,240.34, above the high-volume range that tops out at $1,228.43, but the latest candle was a pin-bar rejection that closed near its low at a recent swing high, with the weekly swing high at $1,249.45 just overhead. The 10-day at $1,200.19, the 20-day at $1,183.00 and the 50-day at $1,181.00 rise beneath, and the 52-week high of $1,292.65 from Aug 19 is the prize above.

Momentum has cooled from hot to firm: RSI eased to 63 from 69, while MACD stays above zero and well over its signal line. On-balance volume is rising with price, the weekly and daily trends point up, and buyers since the Aug 5 earnings are in profit above $1,184.91. Revenue grew 47.7% and profit rose to $7,095.0M from $5,661.0M, and the stock is up 35% over six months. Volume on the down day was 0.87× normal, a quiet pullback, so the setup is a breakout trade: a close over the recent swing high confirms that the rejection candle was a pause, and the run to the 52-week high opens from there.

prose.headline: Molina: buy the triangle-breakout pullback to $206.31 by Oct 23, toward $216.93 by Oct 29, wrong under $202.18.
story: Molina Healthcare has cleared a descending triangle that had held it since May 26, and the breakout retest held the next session. The same week it reclaimed the 50-day at $199.70 on Oct 12, and price now sits at $210.20, above the 10-day at $203.58 and the top of the high-volume range at $208.17. Underneath is a deep floor: a cluster of five levels in the support zone between $199.40 and $204.20, the busiest price at $198.92 and the 20-day at $196.70. The Oct 14 upthrust at the weekly swing high of $214.36 failed, so that shelf and the 20-session high above it are the first resistance.

Every timeframe points up, weekly, daily and hourly, and momentum is behind the breakout: RSI rose to 61 from 58 after a regular bullish divergence, and MACD crossed above zero on Oct 13 and sits well over its signal line. Ten-session volume has run 1.23× normal, and the 20-day VWAP at $197.43 trails under price. The fundamentals are the soft spot, with revenue down 4.8%, profit down to $60.0M from $255.0M and a weak earnings reaction, and the stock lags its sector by 16.8 points over three months. That is why the entry is a pullback into the support zone, not a chase into the upthrust level.

prose.headline: Perrigo: buy $16.09 on its breakout for a measured run to $18.82 by Nov 10, wrong under $15.18.
story: Perrigo has turned a broken stock into a working uptrend. The breakaway gap up on Aug 5 started it, the swings have stepped up since, and price has now closed above the last swing high at $15.69 and the Fibonacci halfway mark at $15.72, with 53% of the fall from $22.21 won back. The averages are stacked beneath, the 10-day at $15.41, the 20-day at $15.00 and the 50-day at $14.30. The 50-day has climbed from $12.60 in a month, while the 200-day sits at $12.39, and a cluster of five levels fills the support zone between $14.90 and $15.15.

The latest session gave back 3.2% on 1.22× normal volume and printed an outside-bar candle that closed near its low, a shakeout at the 20-session high rather than a break, since the close held above the top of the high-volume range at $15.18. RSI cooled to 63 from 71, MACD is still above zero and over its signal line, and the accumulation/distribution line shows a hidden bullish divergence. Profit swung to $74.5M from an $8.4M loss, buyers since the Aug 5 earnings are well in profit above $14.22, and the stock leads the S&P 500 by 51.2 points over three months. Price is stretched 2.6 daily ranges above the 50-day and the October record is weak, which makes this a hold-the-line buy at the top of the range.

prose.headline: Bumble: buy $5.93 as the breakout holds, $6.17 measured target by Nov 13, wrong below $5.81.
story: Bumble has gone nearly vertical. A double bottom and a descending triangle both broke to the upside on heavy volume five sessions ago, the stock gapped up the next day, and it closed at $5.96, a whisker under its 52-week high of $5.98 from Oct 13. The averages are left far behind, with the 10-day at $4.37, the 20-day at $3.49 and the 50-day at $3.09, and the unfilled gap from Oct 13 would only fill back at $3.97. The busiest price at $5.94 sits right under the close, and the weekly swing high at $6.26 is the next shelf above.

Volume has carried it, 1.68× normal on the day and 2.00× over ten sessions, on-balance volume is rising, and the stock leads the S&P 500 by 105.2 points over three months. But the run is stretched to an extreme, 10.7 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than any day of its past year, and RSI sits at 90 with stochastic pinned near the top. MACD is above zero and over its signal line with the gap narrowing. The business is still losing money, a $110.1M loss on revenue down 15.2%, so this is a momentum trade with a tight line, and the buy is a hold near $5.90, just above the busiest price.

prose.headline: Blackbaud: buy the pullback to $51.55 by Oct 23, with $61.18 the weekly target by Nov 30; out under $49.58.
story: Blackbaud is breaking out of a long base inside a rising wedge that started on Apr 29. The Sep 30 spring under $41.50 marked the low, the swings turned up from the last swing low at $40.82, and price has now closed above the last swing high at $49.54 at $53.24, up 3.1% on a bullish engulfing candle. That puts it right under the Fibonacci level at $53.47, with 61% of the fall from $70.71 won back. The averages lag far behind, the 10-day at $47.83, the 20-day at $45.14 and the 50-day at $45.61, which has risen from $42.37 in a month.

Momentum is hot: RSI rose to 80 from 77, MACD is above zero and over its signal line with the gap widening, and two bullish divergences flagged the turn before price did. On-balance volume is rising, the 20-day VWAP at $45.74 and the busiest price at $45.77 sit far below, and the stock leads the S&P 500 by 66.4 points over three months. Profit grew to $35.4M from $26.5M on revenue up 3.0%. The problem is distance: price is stretched 4.5 daily ranges above the 50-day, further than 90% of its past year, so the entry is a pullback to the 2-session low, with the weekly swing high as the target.

prose.headline: Baxter: buy $24.99 on the 50-day shelf for a run to $25.99 by Oct 26, wrong under $24.55.
story: Baxter has pulled back into a layer of support after a strong summer. The swings still step up from the last swing low at $22.56. The latest session held the 50-day at $24.96 and closed at $24.99, with the Fibonacci 38.2% level of the run from $15.73 just below at $24.55. The 10-day at $24.71, the 20-day at $24.17 and the support line near $24.15 add to the floor, and the 200-day at $21.14 is rising far underneath. The 52-week high of $30.00 from Jul 30 came on an exhaustion gap that has since filled.

Momentum has eased without breaking: RSI slipped to 56 from 60, while MACD stays above zero and over its signal line after crossing above zero on Oct 14. Hidden bullish divergences on RSI and money flow say the dip is being bought, though the latest candle was a shooting star that closed near its low and the weekly on-balance volume has diverged lower. Profit rose to $126.0M from $91.0M on revenue up 5.3%, and the stock is up 33% over six months. Holders since the Jul 30 earnings sit 1.4% under their $25.34 average, which is why the objective is the nearby 20-session high rather than the old peak.

prose.headline: Becton Dickinson: buy $190.74 above the high-volume range, aiming at the $195.99 high by Oct 26; out below $187.96.
story: Becton Dickinson is pressing against its highs. The swings have stepped up from the last swing low at $175.20, it set a 52-week high of $195.99 on Oct 16, and the close at $190.74 sits just above the top of the high-volume range at $187.96. The 10-day at $186.84, the 20-day at $183.90 and the 50-day at $184.20 are stacked underneath, and the 50-day has climbed from $175.37 in a month. Buyers since the Aug 6 earnings are in profit above $183.39, and the 200-day is far below at $164.30.

The weekly swing high at $192.08, 1% overhead, is the hurdle: the latest candle left a wick rejection there, and price slipped back under the short-term support line near $194.60. RSI eased to 62 from 64 with a negative divergence that price has not confirmed. MACD stays above zero and over its signal line, on-balance volume is rising, and the pullback came on light volume, 0.76× normal. The stock is up 20% over six months and leads the S&P 500 by 21.6 points over three months, though profit fell to $377.0M from $574.0M. Holding above the high-volume range keeps the buy on, with the recent high as the objective.

story: BlackRock came through its Oct 14 earnings with revenue up 30.6% and profit up to $1,914.0M from $1,593.0M, and the stock reclaimed its 50-day the next day. It now trades at $1,124.60, above the 10-day at $1,090.04, the 20-day at $1,079.00 and the 50-day at $1,106.00. Of the fall from $1,220.00 to $917.40, it has won back 68%. The 200-day at $1,061.00 is flat below, the support line sits near $1,048.00, and the Sep 16 spring marked the floor of the base.

Momentum is turning up: MACD crossed above zero and is over its signal line with the gap widening, and on-balance volume is rising. The latest session was a warning, though, an engulfing candle that swallowed the prior day and closed near its low at a recent swing high. RSI eased to 60 from 64, and stochastic sits at 95. The 52-week high of $1,187.17 from Aug 27 was an upthrust that failed back under, and buyers since the earnings average $1,109.86, just under price. The pullback buy sits at the busiest price, $1,070.49, next to the 20-day VWAP at $1,084.43, with the top of the high-volume range as the objective.

prose.headline: Church & Dwight: buy the dip to $103.19 by Oct 23, run to $105.54 by Oct 29, out under $101.85.
story: Church & Dwight has climbed back within reach of its 52-week high of $106.04 from Feb 24. Price closed at $104.09, above the last swing high at $103.20, after the Sep 11 spring set the low for this run. The averages sit well below, the 10-day at $100.35, the 20-day at $97.81 and the 50-day at $98.31, and the 200-day at $96.82 is rising slowly. The top of the high-volume range at $101.48 and the busiest price at $95.38 mark the support underneath.

RSI eased to 75 from 78 and MACD is above zero and over its signal line. Hidden bullish divergences on the accumulation/distribution line and money flow show buyers stepping in on dips. The risk is the ceiling: the weekly swing high at $104.84 is 1% overhead, and the latest candle was a harami with a wick rejection at a recent swing high. Price is also stretched 3.2 daily ranges above the 50-day, further than 88% of its past year. Profit rose to $202.8M from $191.0M on revenue up 1.6%, and the setup favors buying a dip to the 2-session low over chasing, with the 20-session high as the objective.

prose.headline: Cintas: buy the pullback to $206.42 by Oct 26, then the $215.37 weekly high by Nov 4; wrong under $201.40.
story: Cintas is in a steady uptrend that the September earnings and the Sep 24 spring both reinforced. The swings keep stepping up from the last swing low at $191.10, the stock gapped up last week, and it closed at $212.30, within reach of the 52-week high of $219.17 from Jul 29. The 10-day at $205.60 leads, with the 20-day at $201.10 and the 50-day at $201.20 flat beneath it and the 200-day at $188.90 below that. The gap from last week is still open and fills at $208.78, and the support zone from $199.10 to $201.40 sits on top of the busiest price at $199.72.

Momentum is easing after a strong run: RSI slipped to 68 from 72, and stochastic is pinned near the top. MACD holds above zero and over its signal line, though the gap is narrowing. Underneath, the accumulation/distribution line shows a bullish weekly divergence, on-balance volume is rising, and the pullback came on light volume, 0.74× normal, so sellers are not pressing. Revenue grew 10.9% and profit rose to $551.7M from $491.1M, while the stock is up 19% over six months. Price is stretched 2.9 daily ranges above the 50-day, so the buy is a pullback into the top of the high-volume range at $204.52, with the weekly swing high at $215.37 as the target.

prose.headline: Dollar General: buy a pullback to $128.31 by Oct 23, targeting $136.05 by Nov 2; wrong below $124.70.
story: Dollar General has spent the autumn rebuilding after its slide from the $158.23 high of Feb 26. The Oct 2 spring marked the low, price reclaimed the 20-day and 50-day this month, and the close at $133.27 sits above the support zone from $130.00 to $131.80. The averages have bunched together underneath, the 10-day at $127.99, the 200-day at $126.40, the 20-day at $124.70 and the 50-day at $124.60. The busiest price at $123.16 and the 20-day VWAP at $125.02 sit in the same pocket.

The turn has come quietly: price is moving easily on 0.92× normal volume, and MACD crossed above zero this month and is over its signal line. Hidden bullish divergences on the accumulation/distribution line and money flow show steady buying. RSI eased to 64 from 67. Profit jumped to $550.3M from $411.4M on revenue up 5.2%. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $134.13 and the Fibonacci level at $134.10 are both 1% away, and the upthrust that came with the Aug 27 earnings still caps the chart, so the better buy is a pullback to the 200-day at $126.40, with the 20-session high as the objective.

story: Employers Holdings escaped a descending triangle that had held it since Jul 30. The breakout came on Oct 14 at $49.60, the retest a session later held, and a double bottom finished a session ago; the latest session set a 52-week high of $52.60 before the stock closed at $51.26. The 10-day at $49.98, the 20-day at $49.03 and the 50-day at $49.01 sit together under the breakout level. The 200-day at $45.54 is below them, and the support line near $47.89 has been touched three times.

The high itself drew sellers: the latest candle was a pin-bar rejection at the resistance zone from $51.89 to $52.76, right where the Jul 30 upthrust failed and where the weekly swing high sits at $52.06. RSI is 68, level with the prior session, MACD is above zero and over its signal line, and stochastic is pinned at 100. Revenue fell 10.6% and profit slipped to $29.1M from $29.7M, so the pull here is the chart, not the business. The buy is a dip to the 2-session low, just above the top of the high-volume range at $50.30, with the recent swing high as the objective.
prose.play: Buy $50.39 to $50.70 on a pullback to the 2-session low by Oct 23; the target is $52.59, a recent swing high, by Oct 30, and a daily close under $49.94, the 3-session low, voids the call.
paras: Employers Holdings escaped a descending triangle that had held it since Jul 30. The breakout came on Oct 14 at $49.60, the retest a session later held, and a double bottom finished a session ago; the latest session set a 52-week high of $52.60 before the stock closed at $51.26. The 10-day at $49.98, the 20-day at $49.03 and the 50-day at $49.01 sit together under the breakout level. The 200-day at $45.54 is below them, and the support line near $47.89 has been touched three times.

The high itself drew sellers: the latest candle was a pin-bar rejection at the resistance zone from $51.89 to $52.76, right where the Jul 30 upthrust failed and where the weekly swing high sits at $52.06. RSI is 68, level with the prior session, MACD is above zero and over its signal line, and stochastic is pinned at 100. Revenue fell 10.6% and profit slipped to $29.1M from $29.7M, so the pull here is the chart, not the business. The buy is a dip to the 2-session low, just above the top of the high-volume range at $50.30, with the recent swing high as the objective.
